title: Records and a scored sample catch a model change that returns 200
subtitle: A made-up incident on a real feature, with real model names. The prompt is at version 14.

outcome.title: Fixed: the app requests gemini-2.5-flash, never an alias
lines: 50 of 50 replays pass. The barista case joins the test set.

captions.title: A wrong grade comes back as a success
captions.text: On Monday morning Google points `gemini-flash-latest` at a preview model. The grading feature now marks correct answers wrong. Every call is fast, returns 200 and throws nothing.

captions.title: The wrapper writes one record per call
captions.text: It logs prompt version 14 and the model that answered, `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025`, a real name. It also stores the prompt and reply with names and emails scrubbed, kept 14 days.

captions.title: A second model scores a 2% sample
captions.text: Calls that finished normally enter a random 2% draw and go on a queue. The pinned checker model reads the redacted text, the verdict and a rubric. It answers DISAGREE, stored as 0.

captions.title: The nightly job sees Monday fall below its band
captions.text: The alert line 0.92 sits three standard deviations below the 30-day mean. Monday scores 0.81, so the alert fires at 06:00 Tuesday. The first learner reports come that afternoon.

captions.title: Grouping by version shows the model moved
captions.text: The prompt is version 14 on every call, so no prompt edit caused it. The response model changes on Monday, and answers graded wrong go from 4% to 19%.

captions.title: Pin the model and replay ten times
captions.text: The team requests `gemini-2.5-flash` instead of the alias. The owner replays each of the 5 stored prompts 10 times. All 50 runs pass, and the barista case joins the test set.
